acousticTransducerSpecs.primaryRole: Generates wide standing wave nodal traps with maximum acoustic radiation force for macro-globules (> 3 µm) and initiates secondary Bjerknes clustering.
Creates dense sub-millimeter standing wave planes with high spatial gradient, trapping submicron droplets (0.5–2 µm) that escape lower frequencies.
Specialized high-resolution acoustic trapping for microalgae single cells and submicron nano-liposomes with zero destructive cavitation.

separationMechanisms.equation: F_rad = - (pi * P0^2 * V_p * beta_m / (2 * lambda)) * Phi(beta, rho) * sin(2 * k * x)
separationMechanisms.description: The net time-averaged pressure gradient exerted by a standing acoustic wave on a particle in suspension. Directs particles with negative acoustic contrast factors (fat globules) toward antinodes, and positive contrast particles (cells/sediment) toward nodes.

Inter-particle attractive forces generated by mutual scattering of sound waves between neighboring oscillating droplets. Causes rapid aggregation into macro-clusters, which dramatically increases the effective Stokes rising or settling velocity.

Eckart and Schlichting acoustic boundary streaming creates convective eddies that can disturb nodal particle bands. The dual-frequency phase-cancellation Skid design dampens large-scale circulating eddies, maintaining stable laminar capture bands.

At megasonic frequencies (> 400 kHz), the Blake transient cavitation threshold increases exponentially. The system operates strictly below the transient cavitation limit, preventing hydroxyl radical (•OH) generation and lipid peroxidation.
